_comment: Mirrors /etc/waybeam-link/craft.json on the vehicle at 192.168.2.232, read from the node 2026-08-08. Devourer (air.kind radio) since 2026-08-06; the kernel-monitor shape this file used to carry was stale.

adapters._power_comment: §10.5 offset space. 8812EU craft floor MEASURED at the ground 2026-08-16: 0/-24/-48 qdb read -13/-20/-27 dBm and -72/-96/-128 all pin at -28 with saturated_low true. 14 dB of travel; -48 is the last rung that moves the air, so the ladder's -72 bottom rung is below the floor and kept only because it saturates honestly. Reversibility checked (0/-48/0/-48 repeated within 2 dB). BENCH-LOW for 50 cm geometry — raise before any range or flight test.

downlink FC telemetry ingest — hub telemetry.udp_target points here

air._mcs_probe_comment: §9.4 ARMED on this node. TX-side half only — the schedule is table content hashed into table_version, so this key does nothing unless the table carries a probe block AND every receiver has the identical table. The former "PER-UNIT enablement, do not copy without its own proof" reservation is WITHDRAWN (operator ruling 2026-08-30, Pass 196): stage 0 measured a property of the DIE, not of a dongle, and passed on all three fleet dies (findings 2026-08-08). The enablement is per-die and these dies are licensed, so this key is safe to copy to any craft on a proven die and composes with §15.2 adapters.auto. Since Pass 186 the candidate is clamped to policy.select.max_profile, so a craft at its ceiling flies no probes at all.

select._profile_pin_comment: Read back from the node 2026-08-21. min_profile is 1, not the 2 this file used to carry: a LOWER floor is the more robust value (§9.0 nothing may make demotion harder), so the node's is the one that wins. max_profile 5 is the shipped envelope and the node had drifted DOWN to 4 — which Pass 186 turned from cosmetic into load-bearing, since the probe candidate is now clamped to this pin and a craft pinned at its own rung flies no probes.

venc._active_mode_comment: Read back from the node 2026-08-21; this file said mcs2 while the craft has been running mcs1. Unrelated to §9.4 — recorded here because leaving a known-wrong value in a reference config is how the §6.3b parity gap happened.
